label: confers
definition: A relation between a trait causal node and a trait: asserts that the presence, activity, or state of the subject is what makes the bearing organism able to exhibit the object trait.
traits_addressed: covers 145 causal-graph edges across 114 trait records
observations: Range-correct replacement for RO:0002327 (enables) on TRAIT objects: biolink gives enables the range 'biological process or activity', which a disposition cannot satisfy (TraitMech#302). Subject types observed: BIOLOGICAL_PROCESS 81, GENE_OR_PROTEIN 32, ENVIRONMENTAL_FACTOR 12, QUALITY 5, CELLULAR_LOCALIZATION 5, PATHWAY 4, CHEMICAL 3, MOLECULAR_FUNCTION 2, STATE 1.

label: has electron donor
definition: A relation between a trait or energy-conserving process and a chemical species: asserts that the object supplies the reducing equivalents the subject's electron flow consumes.
traits_addressed: covers 13 causal-graph edges across 13 trait records
observations: Role-bearing sibling of METPO:2007702; restores the donor/acceptor distinction collapsed when 15 edges were reversed onto enables (TraitMech#303). Unlike METPO:2000009 the domain is a causal-graph node rather than microbe, so it carries no organism entailment (TraitMech#301).

label: has electron acceptor
definition: A relation between a trait or energy-conserving process and a chemical species: asserts that the object receives the reducing equivalents the subject's electron flow discharges.
traits_addressed: covers 6 causal-graph edges across 4 trait records
observations: Role-bearing sibling of METPO:2007701. The sharpest TraitMech#303 case is dissimilatory_iron_reduction: all three of its Fe(III) species are terminal electron acceptors per the file's own node descriptions, but once two of them were reversed onto enables by PR #300 nothing in predicate terms records the acceptor role at all. Domain is a causal-graph node, not microbe (TraitMech#301).
